messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: POC plan & risk tracker — BrightLeaf (next steps / success criteria)

Hi Alex — thanks for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery + what we'll own on the Redwood side.

TL;DR
- Proposed POC window: 4 weeks (kickoff 2026-12-20)
- Success criteria (agreed-to ask): latency <200ms p95 on sample traffic, embedding similarity A/B improvement >= 12% vs current baseline, no data retention beyond session scope
- Owners: Marissa (program), Dev (technical lead), Rachel (security/compliance contact), Alex/Priya (BrightLeaf leads)

Attached: BrightLeaf-POC-MA-plan-v1.xlsx (schedule + milestone checklist) and a first-pass risk tracker.

Proposed evaluation plan (high level)
1) Week 0 (pre-kickoff): exchange sample dataset (anonymized), grant test accounts, confirm network egress rules. Owner: Alex/Priya
2) Week 1: model integration + smoke tests; baseline generation from BrightLeaf current endpoint. Owner: Dev
3) Week 2: run evaluation suite (latency, throughput, accuracy on held-out prompts). Owner: Dev + BrightLeaf data team
4) Week 3: iterate on prompts/quantization/batching; verify p95 & embedding delta. Owner: Dev + Marissa
5) Week 4: handoff, success review, contract/next steps. Owner: Marissa/Vivek

Initial risks & mitigations (summary)
- Risk: Data residency / auditability concerns (Priya flagged SOC2 evidence). Mitigation: Rachel will share SOC2 summary + audit logs availability and KMS options.
- Risk: Latency variance on 99th percentile for long context. Mitigation: Dev will test with streaming + dynamic batching; fallback to smaller context profile if needed.
- Risk: Blocking bug in connector for BrightLeaf auth. Mitigation: we will dedicate 4 engineer-hours in Week 0-1 and have an escalation path to Eng leads.

Next steps (please confirm):
- Alex: share anonymized sample set + allow test IPs by EOD 2026-12-17
- Priya: confirm SOC2 evidence recipients (Rachel)
- Dev: produce a one-page POC test plan by 2026-12-18
- Marissa/Vivek: schedule kickoff for 2026-12-20 09:00 PT

Thanks — looking forward.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Alex / Marissa — adding a quick technical note and an attached test-plan (redwood-poc-test-plan.md) with runnable checks. High level answers to Alex's asks: 

- DSA/NDA: legal will be fine with a short addendum; Marissa / Vivek pls loop Legal if you want us to fast-track.
- SSO/SAML: we can support a light SAML flow for a single test user. Timeline: configure/test in Week 0 (2 engineer-hours to configure IdP, 2 hours to validate). We may fall back to API-key-based test user if SAML proves slow to set up.
- Logging retention: we store request-level logs internally for 180 days by default for enterprise; for the POC we can provide a 90-day export of inference logs (request id, timestamp, model, latency, response size) as CSV. Rachel, I can prep the export pipeline if you confirm fields.

Known technical risks & proposed mitigations (from the test-plan):
1) Blocking connector bug (auth handshake) — mitigation: allocate a 4-hour hotfix window in Week 0 and a dedicated escalation to our infra on-call. If unresolved within 24 hours, escalate to Eng manager (Vivek).
2) Model performance delta on long prompts — mitigation: run an early ablation with smaller context length and enable streaming; if p95 still >200ms, we will try quantization profile Q4 and re-run.
3) Data leak concerns with embeddings — mitigation: embeddings used in POC will be pseudo-anonymized and stored only in a scoped test index with TTL 14 days.

I'll attach the test-plan and a checklist for the run.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer
